subject: Per-account PII-redaction & audit-hook request for Pegasus deal
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@pegasusbank.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: DevOps Team <infra@pegasusbank.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood eval — logs & legal replay questions

Hi Jasmine,

Quick follow-up from our legal and infra review. We can move forward with Redwood if you can provide:

- Structured inference logs that preserve the prompt/response schema (JSON) but with PII redacted (names, email addresses, account numbers). Redaction should be deterministic and reversible only with a secure key held by Pegasus (we need a mapping id for replay).
- Token-level audit hooks: for any request we want an export that includes input tokens (redacted), output tokens (redacted), model id/version, snapshot id, timestamp, and a checksum so our legal team can replay the exact interaction later.
- Export formats (CSV + JSON) and S3-compatible export to our bucket or secure transfer via signed URL.
- Retention options per account (30/90/365 days) and an ability to trigger a bulk export for an investigation.

This is a gating security ask for our compliance sign-off. If Redwood can commit to a per-account redaction + snapshotting flow (and share expected latency/throughput impact) we can finalize the contract this week.

I've attached a sample prompt set and our security questionnaire. Happy to jump on a short call with your engineering leads.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Legal Operations
Pegasus Bank

Team — forwarding Pegasus' ask (attached). Short summary: their legal+infosec require schema-preserving logs with deterministic PII redaction + a snapshot id for replay. They need exportability to their S3 and retention options. This is explicit contract gating: legal says no final sign-off without it.

Ask of Product/Eng: can we scope a minimal implementation that:
- Produces structured log entries for each request with fields: snapshot_id, model_id, timestamp, input_schema, redacted_input, redacted_output, checksum.
- Uses a reversible mapping for redaction controlled by Pegasus (we can implement a salt-based pseudonymization or HSM-backed tokenization — they prefer customer-managed key).
- Supports per-account retention policies and an on-demand bulk export API.

Constraints & considerations I expect you'll flag: latency impact, storage costs, security review, and whether this is hosted-only or also for Dedicated/Private.

Proposed next steps:
1) Product quick feasibility note (2 business days) + high level ETA for a canary.
2) If feasible, we propose a Dedicated-canary (Pegasus will take a dedicated pool) to limit blast radius.
3) Security review with their team (they want a 30 min sync).

They sign if we can give a plausible timeline this week. Please reply with: feasibility (yes/no), rough effort (small/medium/large), estimated calendar ETA, and any blockers.

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pegasus eval — logs & legal replay questions

Thanks for the context and the sample prompts. High-level technical assessment below. TL;DR: feasible as scoped but requires a small engineering project plus security/HSM integration.

Feasibility points:
- Schema-preserving logs: straightforward. We can add a logging pipeline that emits a structured JSON per request.
- Deterministic PII redaction with customer control: doable but requires one of the following: (a) customer-managed encryption key (CKM) for reversible pseudonymization stored in HSM/KMS; (b) salted irreversible hashing (not reversible, so fails legal replay requirement). Pegasus explicitly requires reversible mapping; so we need CKM/HSM integration (we already have KMS hooks in Private/Dedicated). For Hosted we can support CMK via an integration flow (we'll need legal/infra sign-off).
- Snapshot id + checksum: no problem — we can compute a canonical representation and checksum and persist snapshot metadata in our audit table.
- Export API + S3 delivery: trivial design; needs infra work to provision signed transfer paths for their bucket.

Non-functional tradeoffs:
- Latency: extra redaction step + KMS calls (if reversible) will add ~5–12% p50/p95 depending on KMS locality. We can mitigate with caching of tokens signed by the CMK but that increases statefulness.
- Storage/Cost: storing full redacted token streams per request increases storage costs. Need pricing discussion with finance.
- Security review: mandatory. We will need PEG to sign data processing addendum and KMS access model.

Estimate and proposed plan:
- Implementation effort: 2 backend engineers + 1 infra engineer + 1 security reviewer. Estimated calendar: 3 weeks to first internal canary, 5–6 weeks for hardened canary with export paths.
- Minimum viable canary (2–3 weeks): schema logging + snapshot id + salted pseudonymization (non-reversible) behind a feature flag for Pegasus-only — useful for initial compliance sign-off but may not satisfy their replay requirement.
- Full reversible flow (customer CMK): 5–6 weeks including security review and infra changes.

Questions / blockers for Sales:
1) Is Pegasus willing to accept an initial non-reversible canary while we build CMK flow?
2) Which retention window(s) are required (30/90/365)? We need this to size storage and exports.
3) Do they require Hosted support or will they be on Dedicated/Private? CMK reversible mapping is easiest on Dedicated/Private.

Link to the internal design stub: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XyZ-redaction-design-stub (internal)

-Markus
Product Lead, Observability & Compliance
Redwood Inference

-- note: internal assessment; security to schedule follow-up once we confirm approach

Markus — really helpful, thank you. Forwarding your notes to Laura (cc'd) so they can weigh in. Quick replies to your questions:

1) Pegasus' legal is adamant about reversible mapping for replay. Non-reversible will not pass their compliance gate. They did note they are open to a short-term trade: a limited-scope non-reversible canary for functional testing, but legal sign-off requires CMK reversible mapping.
2) Retention: they want optional 30/90/365 per-account; for the deal they will take 90 days for all activity initially.
3) Deployment: Pegasus prefers Dedicated. They want guarantees on export and an ability to bring the same feature to Private later.

Next steps (proposed):
- Product/Eng: please confirm you can commit to the 5–6 week CMK reversible path for a Dedicated canary. If yes, can you provide a target calendar date for the canary start?
- Security: can you schedule a 30-min sync with Pegasus legal/security this week? They prefer Wed or Thu mornings PST.
- Sales: I'll update the HubSpot deal and tell the customer we can commit to a Dedicated canary with CMK reversible mapping and 90-day retention — pending a light security review.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/23452345/PEG-ENT-2027-0421
